book.why: The only name two members picked, for different reasons: Ophelia for the FDA-approval part of the healthcare breakout and Cecil as the only cheap way into healthcare at 17.7x.

Ophelia's most direct way to own money moving into healthcare (about 12% of XLV, at a 52-week closing high, lowest volatility of her three healthcare leaders), and its 95% EPS growth weakens Cecil's objection to its 39.9x multiple.
Ophelia's energy call rests on a real supply cut, and XLE's -0.38 correlation to SPY makes it the book's hedge against the jump in the 10Y that both members fear from a hot PCE or a hawkish Warsh.
Cecil's cheapest sound business (11.6x, EPS +10.1%) is his own hedge against that same rising-yield risk, because its float earns more as reinvestment yields climb.
Cecil's low-volatility defensive (1.88% weekly, 17.2x) is also supported by Ophelia's staples read, so it cushions the book if NVDA disappoints on Wednesday.

rationale: REGN is the only name two members picked, so it gets the 30% cap; with LLY, half the book is in healthcare. Both members name the same main risk, a hot PCE or hawkish Warsh pushing the 10Y toward 4.75-5%, and each brings a different hedge, so the book holds both (COP, PGR) plus PEP, and it stays fully invested because the defense is already in the names. Marky's five are all left out: all five have weekly MACD histograms still falling and 12-week returns between -8.3% and +3.2%, which looks like broken channels rather than pullbacks.
